title: The oil spill spreading along the UAE coast
credits: Photos: Karthik B K, Anders Marlowe, Nathan Dumlao / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: An oil spill off the coast of the United Arab Emirates is growing, and more beaches are closing.
Satellite images from the EU's Copernicus programme show dark oil spreading at sea and along the coast near Umm Al Quwain.
Umm Al Quwain has closed all its beaches and coastal areas.
Ras Al Khaimah has closed all beaches until further notice, and Sharjah has shut access to Al Hamriyah beach.
UAE authorities have not named the ship responsible.
But experts told Reuters it is the tanker Gem Number Two, which shipping sources say was hit by an unidentified projectile earlier this month.
The UAE's environment ministry says containment work is under way, along with an environmental assessment.
A water expert at New York University Abu Dhabi called it a serious environmental concern.
According to the IUCN, the UAE's waters are home to more than five hundred fish species, as well as dolphins and sea turtles.
October has been the worst month yet for attacks on ships around the Strait of Hormuz.
The Gulf's beaches and wildlife are now paying a price for the war at sea.
